description: TriOrbit is a three-member IT team participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge – Colombo. We are passionate about software development, creative problem-solving, data, and building practical technology solutions. Our goal is to collaborate, learn, and develop an engaging solution using NASA’s open data and resources.
summary:
TriOrbit is an interactive lunar survival simulator designed to teach children aged 7–12 about the challenges of living on the Moon.

Players become mission commanders responsible for keeping three astronauts alive across five simulated days. With only two maintenance actions per day, they must carefully balance Oxygen, Power, Water, Food, and Radiation Risk while operating four interconnected lunar habitat systems.

The game incorporates authentic historical Solar Energetic Particle observations from NASA's DONKI database, including an event recorded by the STEREO A spacecraft on May 11, 2024. Players experience how space weather can influence mission decisions while learning that the game's resource values are simplified educational simulations.

Through interactive gameplay, scientific explanations, mission debriefs, and instant replay, TriOrbit encourages systems thinking, problem-solving, and curiosity about space exploration.

Built with Next.js, React, and TypeScript, it provides an accessible learning experience without requiring accounts or installations.
details:
The Problem

Living on the Moon requires careful management of oxygen, electricity, water, food, and radiation protection. These systems are interconnected, yet younger students often learn about space exploration through passive explanations rather than practical decision-making.

TriOrbit addresses this challenge by transforming lunar habitat management into an interactive educational game for children aged 7–12.

Our Solution

TriOrbit places players in command of Lunar Base Alpha, a simulated lunar outpost supporting three astronauts.

The mission lasts five simulated days. Each day, the player receives two maintenance actions and must decide how best to maintain the lunar habitat.

Four interactive facilities support the mission:

  • Solar Power Station: Restores electrical power by maintaining solar panels.
  • Life Support Habitat: Produces oxygen while consuming power and water.
  • Hydroponics Greenhouse: Supports food production and water recycling.
  • Shielded Regolith Bunker: Reduces simulated radiation risk.

Five resource gauges help players monitor Oxygen, Power, Water, Food, and Radiation Risk. Every decision affects the remaining resources, helping children understand the importance of planning and balancing competing needs.

NASA Data Integration

TriOrbit integrates authentic historical space weather information from NASA's Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information (DONKI).

The Day 2 solar storm scenario references a Solar Energetic Particle event observed by NASA's STEREO A spacecraft on May 11, 2024.

The game also includes simulated habitat emergencies involving electrical systems and hydroponic irrigation.

To maintain scientific accuracy, TriOrbit clearly distinguishes authentic NASA observations from fictional mission events. All resource values and radiation-risk scores are simplified educational game points, not real measurements of lunar conditions or astronaut radiation exposure.

A dedicated NASA Science section presents five educational topics with links to official scientific resources.

Technology and Implementation

TriOrbit was developed using:

  • Next.js and React for the interactive application.
  • TypeScript for the deterministic simulation engine.
  • Tailwind CSS for responsive user interface design.
  • NASA DONKI API integration through a server-side API route.
  • Verified historical NASA data as a fallback when the upstream service is unavailable.
  • Web Audio API for optional interactive sound effects.
  • Vercel for web hosting.

The game supports desktop and mobile browsers, keyboard navigation, and local progress restoration. No login or database is required.

Innovation and Educational Impact

TriOrbit combines interactive lunar habitat management, real historical NASA space weather data, and child-friendly resource decisions in one accessible experience.

Instead of only answering science questions, students learn by experimenting with operational choices.

At the end of the mission, players receive a success or failure debrief with feedback on their strategy. Instant replay encourages them to explore different approaches.

Our goal is to help young learners understand resource conservation, space weather, systems thinking, and the challenges of future Moon missions.

Project Links

Live Application: https://triorbit-lunar-mission.vercel.app/

Source Code: https://github.com/abhi190503/triorbit-lunar-mission

Limitations

TriOrbit is a simplified educational simulation rather than a physically accurate lunar habitat engineering model. NASA spacecraft observations provide historical scientific context, while gameplay calculations are deterministic teaching models.
